chunks.text: Retrieval-Augmented Generation combines a vector database with a large language model. The vector database stores embeddings of source passages; at query time, the user's question is embedded and the most similar passages are retrieved as context for the LLM, which then generates an answer grounded in those passages.

Qdrant is a production-grade vector database written in Rust. It supports HNSW-based approximate nearest neighbor search, payload filtering, and a REST and gRPC API. RAGStack uses Qdrant as its primary dense retrieval engine.

Hybrid retrieval combines dense vector search with sparse BM25 keyword search. RAGStack fuses the two ranked lists with Reciprocal Rank Fusion, then optionally reranks the top candidates with a cross-encoder model before passing them to the LLM.

Apptainer, formerly known as Singularity, is the HPC-friendly container runtime. Unlike Docker, it runs rootless by default, has no long-lived daemon, and integrates with shared filesystems on cluster nodes. RAGStack's apptainer scripts start Qdrant, Elasticsearch, Neo4j, Postgres, and Redis as instances on the host network.

Every container's writable directories are bind-mounted to host paths under apptainer/data/, so service state persists across down/up cycles. Elasticsearch and Neo4j config directories are seeded from the image on first run because both services write configuration files at startup.
